## 2026-07-25 — KLEBER-APP-OPERATIONAL-STABILIZATION-BATCH-02-R1 — feat: add Pedido date and controlled numbering

- **Gate.** The architect issued `KLEBER-APP-OPERATIONAL-STABILIZATION-BATCH-02-R1` as a bounded database plus Pedido UI implementation with local validation and one authorized shared-development migration apply, naming target `ucrjtfswnfdlxwtmxnoo`, expected starting terminal `db/88` and authorized final terminal `db/89`. The order explicitly prohibited production, Vercel, `main` and manual deployment. Two binding rulings were issued and applied verbatim: (1) `public.pedidos.data_pedido` is NOT a naming collision with the pre-existing `public.ordens_compra_fio.data_pedido`, because column names are table-scoped and both meanings are clear in their owning tables, so the Pedido column was NOT renamed; (2) placing Tipo before Modelo inside a modal does NOT satisfy the requested placement — on `#/pedidos/novo` both must be selectable directly in the item row, and the full item entity must not remain inside an editing modal.
- **Accepted checkpoint.** Implementation `65e1278c4ab70244ce707954416a3892c54577bb`, parent `f7f38774e6bf63e3e4f589cd786a6119789b8848` (BATCH-01). Fifteen paths changed: `db/89_pedido_commercial_date_and_number_control.sql` and `js/screens/pedido-item-row-editor.js` created; `js/screens/pedido-form.js`, `js/screens/pedido-itens-edit.js`, `js/screens/cliente-pedido-form.js`, `js/screens/pedido-edit.js`, `js/screens/pedido-detail-data.js`, `index.html`, `tests/pedido-form.smoke.js`, `tests/ordem-compra-c3d-deploy.smoke.js`, `tests/manta-route-ui.smoke.js`, `tests/responsive-layout.smoke.js` and `tests/document-decision-command-contract.test.js` modified; `tests/pedido-batch02-surfaces.smoke.js` and `tests/pedido-commercial-date-and-number-invariant.mjs` created.
- **Database semantics.** `db/89` is forward-only and leaves `db/01`-`db/88` untouched. It adds `public.pedidos.data_pedido` in the required sequence — nullable column, backfill from `criado_em` projected onto the Brazil business calendar `(criado_em AT TIME ZONE 'America/Sao_Paulo')::date`, default `(now() AT TIME ZONE 'America/Sao_Paulo')::date`, then `NOT NULL` — with the backfill touching only NULL rows so a replay never rewrites a date the operator has already corrected. `criado_em` remains the immutable technical timestamp and is never again read as the commercial date. It adds `pedidos_numero_positivo_chk (numero > 0)`, the `pedidos_numero_immutability_guard` trigger that refuses any UPDATE changing `numero` while a same-value UPDATE does not even fire it, and the `pedidos_numero_sequence_sync` trigger that advances the identity sequence forward-only when an inserted explicit number exceeds it, serialized by `pg_advisory_xact_lock` and touching no table row, so it is a LEAF in the db/88 global lock order. `GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY` lets an explicit value skip the sequence, so without this synchronization a manual high number becomes a latent `UNIQUE` collision surfacing years later to a different user; the synchronizer converts that into a gap. Increasing-but-not-gapless numbering is the accepted contract, gapless numbering is NOT attempted, and `UNIQUE(numero)` remains the final concurrency backstop.
- **Environment identity.** Target `ucrjtfswnfdlxwtmxnoo`, database `postgres`, PostgreSQL 17.6. Positive proof: `inet_server_addr()` `2600:1f18:38df:9501:5625:752d:c0e9:7c06` equals the AAAA record of `db.ucrjtfswnfdlxwtmxnoo.supabase.co`. Negative proof: production `gqmpsxkxynrjvidfmojk` resolves to `2600:1f11:c29:8b01:dd6a:78ed:ae5a:78ce` and forbidden `bhgifjrfagkzubpyqpew` to `2600:1f1e:dbb:f602:8af4:6494:36fa:5896`; neither was ever connected to.
- **Pre-apply gates.** Starting terminal was exactly `db/88` with `db/89` absent and zero partially installed objects: `data_pedido` absent, `pedidos_numero_positivo_chk` absent, both triggers absent and both guard functions absent. The db/89 data gate was reproduced read-only with zero violations — no Pedido carried a null or non-positive `numero` — so it was satisfied on real data and no row was repaired or reinterpreted.
- **Applied migration.** Exactly one, once, from its canonical file via the repository's canonical mechanism (Supabase MCP `apply_migration`, one canonical file-stem per call, no `execute_sql` used for DDL): `89_pedido_commercial_date_and_number_control`. Final terminal `db/89`, recorded exactly once in `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` (40 migrations total). The apply payload was proved byte-identical to the committed blob before execution — worktree and `HEAD` SHA-256 both `1ba2bd1a4442becfa846aa03f224922b145ec988b603e55d0193efa38702400c`, 10 501 bytes.

No RLS policy, grant, existing constraint, existing trigger or existing RPC changed, and neither new function was granted to `PUBLIC` or `anon`.
- **Live validation.** One bounded transaction ending in `ROLLBACK`, touching only synthetic rows, proved five of five required behaviours: automatic numbering allocated `68` above the starting sequence `67`; `data_pedido` defaulted to `2026-07-25`, equal to the Brazil-local date; an available manual number `1` was accepted exactly as supplied; a duplicate manual number was refused with `23505`; renumbering was refused with `23514` by the immutability guard; and a same-value `numero` UPDATE was accepted. The manual number `1`, being below the sequence, did not move it, confirming the forward-only rule on the live environment. Concurrency was deliberately not drilled on shared development — the disposable-cluster harness owns that proof.
- **Zero residue.** After the rollback `public.pedidos` holds exactly its single pre-existing real row (`numero = 67`), zero rows carry the synthetic numbers `1`, `68` or `999999`, `pedido_itens` is unchanged at 9 rows, and zero rows have a null `data_pedido`. No real business row was created, edited, migrated or repaired. The identity sequence advanced `67 -> 68`: `setval` is non-transactional, so the automatic insert's consumption survives the rollback. This is the single accepted gap and is explicitly permitted by the order.
- **Local validation.** `db/89` is proved on a disposable local PostgreSQL 18.4 cluster by the new `tests/pedido-commercial-date-and-number-invariant.mjs`, which never connects to any shared or remote host and destroys its cluster before exit: clean `db/01`-`db/89` apply; zero schema, constraint, trigger, function and grant drift on re-apply, with an operator-corrected date preserved across the replay; Brazil-local backfill proved with instants chosen so a naive `criado_em::date` in UTC would yield the wrong calendar day and fail; default, explicit value and `NOT NULL`; automatic numbering; exact manual number; duplicate, zero and negative rejection; a manual high number advancing the sequence so the next automatic number cannot collide; a manual low unused number never moving it backwards; immutability with same-value acceptance; and TWO real distinct psql sessions proving that concurrent inserts of the same manual number yield exactly one Pedido, the loser receiving a unique violation, with zero duplicated `numero` anywhere.
- **Accepted product behavior.** The admin new-Pedido header is `Número do pedido` -> `Data do pedido` -> `Prazo desejado`. The number is optional and admin-creation-only: blank keeps automatic allocation, a supplied number is persisted verbatim, and an occupied number shows `Este número de pedido já está em uso.` without ever being silently replaced by an automatic one; the UI availability check is advisory and the database `UNIQUE` constraint is authoritative. `Data do pedido` is required, defaults to the browser's local date, persists to `pedidos.data_pedido` and is editable later through the header-edit surface. The item modal was REMOVED: `Adicionar item` now appends an editable row, and Tipo and Modelo are inline dropdowns in the row itself, in the canonical order `Img | Tipo | Modelo | Cores | Largura | Metragem | Observação | Ações`. Modelo stays disabled until Tipo is chosen, lists only models whose `modelos.tipo_produto` matches, and changing Tipo clears `modelo_id`, colors, width and preview. The same Tipo-before-Modelo rule governs saved-Pedido item editing and client-facing creation; the client form carries `data_pedido` and never exposes the internal Pedido number; header editing shows `numero` as read-only context and never places it in the update payload. `pedido_itens` is semantically unchanged and still stores exactly `pedido_id`, `modelo_id`, `metros`, `ordem` and `observacao` — the product type is never persisted redundantly and `modelo_id` remains the only product identity.

- **Database semantics.** `db/90` is forward-only and leaves `db/01`-`db/89` untouched. It adds exactly one read-only RPC, `public.consultar_proximo_numero_pedido() RETURNS BIGINT`, and touches no table, column, constraint, trigger, policy, existing function, existing grant or row. It answers one question — which number the next automatic Pedido would receive — so the admin creation form can OPEN with that number visible instead of an empty `Automático` placeholder. The candidate is derived from the identity sequence state: `pg_sequence_last_value` plus `seqincrement`/`seqstart` read from `pg_catalog.pg_sequence` rather than the `pg_sequences` view, because the view filters by caller privilege while the catalog returns the real definition. A virgin sequence (`is_called = false`, `pg_sequence_last_value` NULL) correctly yields `seqstart`. A fail-closed pre-requisite gate refuses to install if `public.is_admin()`, the identity sequence or `pedidos_numero_positivo_chk` is absent.
- **Why not MAX(numero)+1.** `MAX(pedidos.numero)+1` is wrong on three paths this system deliberately allows: an explicit HIGH manual number already advanced the sequence through the db/89 synchronizer, so the sequence can sit far ahead of any surviving row; a rolled-back or compensated creation consumed a sequence value no row will ever carry, so `MAX` lags permanently; and numbering gaps are accepted by design, so `MAX+1` would try to refill a gap the sequence has already passed, colliding with nothing today and with a real Pedido tomorrow. Reading the sequence is the only answer that matches what the database would actually do.
- **Consultation reserves nothing and consumes nothing.** The function never calls `nextval`, `setval` or `currval` — proved on the applied object by stripping `--` comments from `pg_get_functiondef` and matching word-boundary patterns, since the comments themselves name what the body refuses to do. Opening the form therefore burns no Pedido number no matter how many forms are abandoned. The returned value is ADVISORY, not a reservation: nothing is locked, and `UNIQUE(pedidos.numero)` remains the authority that resolves any race with `23505`.
- **Controlled concurrent conflict.** The two occupied-number paths are distinct and neither reallocates silently. If the untouched automatic suggestion is taken between form opening and submission, the UI detects the unique violation, calls the RPC again, replaces the field with the fresh candidate, and states both the number that became occupied and its replacement — `O número 69 acabou de ser usado por outro pedido. Nova sugestão: 70.` — without creating the Pedido; the operator must submit again. If the operator had manually changed the number, the typed value is PRESERVED and the message is exactly `Este número de pedido já está em uso.`. If the RPC is unavailable the field stays empty under a controlled `Sugestão indisponível` state, manual entry still works, and the identity column allocates; the word `Automático` never returns and no `MAX` fallback exists.
